producer_report.summary: A dependency on a rejected, failed, timed-out or stale job with no landed retry now holds the dependent item. `Plan::build_with(entries, history)` holds it and everything that depends on it, and lists each in `Plan::refused` with a reason naming the dependency and an empty `missing`. `Plan::build(entries)` still works with no history, so existing callers are unchanged. A dependency is met when the job landed, or when a landed job reaches it through "try again on <job>" links, including chains and loops. Dropped, declined, abandoned and unknown ids still count as met. `reading::job_history` builds the history from the records, `Steps::job_history` defaults to empty and `RealSteps` overrides it, so `athena plan` and drain both get the rule through `Drain::prepare`. `display::plan` prints a `held` line for such a refusal. One thing outside the plan: a retry job's text names the job it retries, so it listed that job as a dependency and would have held itself. I added `Ending::Other` and a rule that an item linked as the retry of a dependency is not held by it, and the unit test and the real-records test both cover it. Full `cargo test --locked` was run once and came back without a failure exit code, but I could not read its output (see open_issues).

open_issues: Departure from the plan: `Ending::Other` and the `retries` exemption were added, with `job_history` listing every request job. The plan's history held only finished jobs, and without the exemption a retry job would have been held by its own dependency.
Departure from the plan: the real-records test is in tests/drain.rs, not tests/job_plan.rs, for the helper reason in the plan.
Full `cargo test --locked` output could not be read; Athena's recorded run is the authority.

A job re-asked in other words, with no 'try again on <job>' text (as in the request's own example for 5c0p), has no retry link and does not release the item; only a text link counts, as the plan chose.
Drain builds the plan once at its start, so a retry that lands during the run releases a held item only at the next plan or drain.
A dependent of an item refused for an incomplete plan is still ordered, as before; this is not changed.
mistakes: The first test draft did a second `go` on the retry, which the plan stage had already read. The test panicked with 'already closed (landed)'. I fixed it.
The first test draft used `[retry.clone()]` in `assert_eq!`, which clippy rejected. I fixed it.

I ran the full suite with unfiltered output, and the harness persisted it outside my working directory where I could not read it. I could not re-run the suite, since the brief allows it once, so I inferred the pass from the exit status.
learnings: `reading::plan_entry` makes an item depend on every job id named in its text. So a retry request ('try again on X') depends on X, and a naive hold rule would hold every retry by the job it retries. The rule needed an exemption for an item that is itself linked as the retry of the dependency.
`athena.go` on a job that `drain::plan` already read runs it directly. A second `go` fails with 'already closed (landed)'.
Clippy in this toolchain rejects `[x.clone()]` compared with a Vec in `assert_eq!` (`cloned_ref_to_slice_refs`). Use `[x.as_str()]`.
Bash cannot run `tail`, pipes or heredocs. A tool result saved outside the working directory cannot be read by Read or Grep.
